findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt.
Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
The parties intend to allow 3 rounds of ordinary revisions for the principal creative Deliverables. Client may submit an unlimited number of questions about a Deliverable during the review period.
Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time upon 20 days' written notice, and Client will pay for all work performed through the effective termination date.
The aggregate liability of either party arising from this Agreement is capped at USD 35,000, except to the extent a different limitation is required by applicable law.

findings.explanation: Net 30 payment terms require waiting a full month after invoicing, creating cash flow gaps for a freelancer managing ongoing operational expenses.
findings.suggested_change: Propose shortening the payment term to Net 15 or upon receipt of invoice.

findings.quoted_text: Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
findings.explanation: Permitting 'minor clarifications' via informal communication channels invites scope creep as clients frequently stretch the definition of minor tweaks.
findings.suggested_change: Require all modifications and clarifications to be formally documented and agreed upon in writing before work proceeds.

findings.quoted_text: The parties intend to allow 3 rounds of ordinary revisions for the principal creative Deliverables. Client may submit an unlimited number of questions about a Deliverable during the review period.
findings.explanation: Using soft phrasing like 'intend to allow' rather than a hard contractual limit, combined with unlimited questions, can lead to endless revision loops disguised as inquiries.
findings.suggested_change: Replace 'intend to allow' with a strict maximum limit of 3 revision rounds and clarify that excessive inquiries requiring rework will incur additional charges.

findings.quoted_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time upon 20 days' written notice, and Client will pay for all work performed through the effective termination date.
findings.explanation: Termination for convenience on short notice allows the client to cancel after the freelancer has turned down other work, paying only for prorated time without compensation for lost project value.
findings.suggested_change: Include a kill fee or a minimum commitment percentage to compensate the freelancer for canceled work.

findings.quoted_text: The aggregate liability of either party arising from this Agreement is capped at USD 35,000, except to the extent a different limitation is required by applicable law.
findings.explanation: The total project fee is USD 24,875, but the liability cap is set significantly higher at USD 35,000, exposing the freelancer to losses exceeding the total revenue of the project.
findings.suggested_change: Cap liability at the total fees actually paid by the client under this Agreement.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello, thank you for sharing the agreement. I have reviewed it and propose the following adjustments: - Regarding the payment terms in the agreement, waiting a full month creates cash flow gaps, so I propose shortening the payment term to Net 15 or upon receipt of invoice. - Regarding the relevant clause on communications, informal channels invite scope creep, so I propose requiring all modifications and clarifications to be formally documented and agreed upon in writing before work proceeds. - Regarding the revision clause, soft phrasing can lead to endless revision loops, so I propose replacing this with a strict maximum limit of 3 revision rounds and clarifying that excessive inquiries requiring rework will incur additional charges. - Regarding the termination clause, short notice without compensation can impact lost value, so I propose including a kill fee or a minimum commitment percentage to compensate for canceled work. - Regarding the liability cap in the relevant clause, the current limit exposes me to losses exceeding total revenue, so I propose capping liability at the total fees actually paid by the client under the agreement. Let me know if these updates work for you. Best regards,
